title: Powers of 10 and exponents: worked examples (10 questions)

questions.q: Look at Worked Example 1. In 10⁵, what is the exponent? [img:pow-ex1]
questions.why: The exponent is the small raised number, so in 10⁵ it is 5.

questions.q: Look at Worked Example 2. What is 10² as a regular number? [img:pow-ex2]
Now you try: what is 10³ as a regular number? Use Example 2 to help. (Commas are okay.) [img:pow-ex2]
Look at Worked Example 3. How many zeros are in 10⁶ when you write it as a regular number? [img:pow-ex3]
questions.why: The exponent matches the number of zeros, so 10⁶ has 6 zeros (1,000,000).

questions.q: What is 10⁴ as a regular number? (Commas are okay.) [img:pow-ex3]
questions.why: The exponent is 4, so write a 1 and then 4 zeros: 10,000.

questions.q: Look at Worked Example 4. Write 10,000 as a power of 10. Type just the exponent. [img:pow-ex4]
questions.why: 10,000 has 4 zeros after the 1, so it is 10⁴.

questions.q: 10 × 10 × 10 × 10 × 10 can be written as 10 to what exponent? [img:pow-ex2]
questions.why: Five 10s are multiplied, so the exponent is 5: 10⁵ = 100,000.
More zeros means a bigger number: 10⁴ = 10,000, 10³ = 1,000, 10² = 100.

questions.q: Look at Worked Example 5. Maya says 10³ = 30. Is she correct? [img:pow-ex5]
Maya's mistake: she did 10 × 3. What is 10³ really equal to? (Commas are okay.) [img:pow-ex5]
